report.title: Exact PCG state, output and advance for all four generator types
report.explanation: For rand_pcg 0.10.2, the four state getters return their stored word. The three LCG stream getters return increment>>1; from_state preserves its input state and stores increment=(stream<<1) OR 1, discarding the highest stream bit. Their new constructors initialize state=((input_state+increment)*multiplier+increment) with modular arithmetic; the multipliers are 6364136223846793005, 47026247687942121848144207491837523525 and 15750249268501108917 respectively. Mcg128Xsl64::new stores input_state OR 1. Native output proofs retain Lcg64Xsh32::try_next_u32 and both word widths for the three 128-bit types. The XSL-RR variants permute the newly advanced state; CM-DXSM permutes the old state then advances. Their 32-bit methods return the low 32 bits of the 64-bit result with the same final state. Original Result::map and conversion closures are body-extracted. Mcg128Xsl64::advance additionally terminates normally for every u128 delta and every internal u128 state, returning state=M^delta*initial_state modulo 2^128, M=47026247687942121848144207491837523525. A well-founded halving-loop proof connects the original body to this ordinary power specification, covering all deltas without an artificial execution bound. These twenty-five direct original-body API guarantees apply under default and serde because the selected official translations are byte-identical; the serde implementations themselves remain unproved. Each of the three LCG advance methods also terminates normally for every full-width delta, state and increment, preserving the stored increment and producing exactly delta repetitions of the ordinary modular affine step x↦M*x+increment. An independent linear recurrence specifies this behavior; a generic affine-composition proof connects the original binary algorithm to it. Increments need not be odd for this state-transform identity. Separate Kani evidence calls the unchanged Mcg128Xsl64::from_seed and public state getter for every sixteen-byte seed. Its state equals the independently decoded little-endian u128 seed OR 1 (242 successful checks under each of default and serde). The exact rand_core 0.10.0 and serde 1.0.228 dependency lock is retained. This is a separate Kani body guarantee, not another Aeneas machine claim or a formal cross-tool equivalence proof.

report.explanation: For rand_xorshift 0.5.0, the Aeneas proof establishes the exact try_next_u32 word and state update for every four-u32 state, using three explicit std wrapping-operator models. With t=x XOR (x << 11), r=w XOR (w >> 19) XOR t XOR (t >> 8); the returned value is Ok(r) and state becomes (y,z,w,r), using 32-bit logical operations. A separate Lean theorem derives preservation of a nonzero state from this exact transition. report.title: Integer From conversions and generic bitwise result preservation
report.explanation: For endian-type 0.2.0, six generic BigEndian/ LittleEndian bitwise methods preserve the underlying operator result. Sixty integer From method bodies additionally implement exact identity or byte reversal under explicitly supplied x86_64 little-endian scalar-operation models. LittleEndian construction and conversion to an integer preserve the stored word; BigEndian construction and conversion to an integer reverse its bytes; cross-wrapper conversion reverses the stored word. These contracts cover every bit pattern of u16/u32/u64/u128/usize and i16/i32/i64/i128/isize. Pointer-sized Lean theorems explicitly require System.Platform.numBits=64. Original source and Cargo.toml are unchanged. Fifty executable external-operation models compose official byte primitives and are proved against independent bitvector specifications; Kani separately checks native Rust operations against explicit reversed-byte references for all inputs. Separate ordinary Kani harnesses directly check forty concrete integer byte APIs (ten harnesses, 220 checks) and sixty integer instantiations of six slice methods (1030 checks, including 180 specification assertions and 20 unsupported-path guards). The slice checks are limited to initialized, correctly aligned exact-length repr(C) leading-field buffers with arbitrary contents and replacement values; they do not establish arbitrary-T, arbitrary allocation-context, invalid/short/misaligned-buffer, or Rust aliasing guarantees. These supplemental Kani checks are not among the 66 Aeneas machine claims.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, Charon/Aeneas, official scalar/byte primitives, Lean kernel, Kani and CBMC are trusted. Fifty native-endian std-operation models are explicitly supplied. Their Rust byte formulas and official Lean byte primitives are connected by review, not a mechanically checked cross-language theorem; std operator bodies are not independently proved in Lean. Kani and extraction use different Rust nightlies. The six bitwise results quantify arbitrary underlying operator dictionaries without proving user callback bodies. All 66 API contracts and 50 model specifications use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound as transitive axioms.
report.limitations: Coverage is limited to six bitwise methods and sixty concrete integer From implementations on the stated target/model domain. The forty-six byte/slice APIs and their unsafe layout/validity/aliasing obligations are not covered by these Aeneas claims. No generic arbitrary-T memory-safety, other target, endian, or pointer-width claim is established. Derived standard-trait methods are excluded. Remaining trait/default/blanket behavior is not verified. Type-specialized Rust identities and any erased server catalogue keys must be distinguished.

Sixty integer From method bodies additionally implement exact identity or byte reversal under explicitly supplied x86_64 little-endian scalar-operation models. LittleEndian construction and conversion to an integer preserve the stored word; BigEndian construction and conversion to an integer reverse its bytes; cross-wrapper conversion reverses the stored word. These contracts cover every bit pattern of u16/u32/u64/u128/usize and i16/i32/i64/i128/isize. Pointer-sized Lean theorems explicitly require System.Platform.numBits=64. Original source and Cargo.toml are unchanged. Fifty executable external-operation models compose official byte primitives and are proved against independent bitvector specifications; Kani separately checks native Rust operations against explicit reversed-byte references for all inputs. Separate ordinary Kani harnesses directly check forty concrete integer byte APIs (ten harnesses, 220 checks) and sixty integer instantiations of six slice methods (1030 checks, including 180 specification assertions and 20 unsupported-path guards). The slice checks are limited to initialized, correctly aligned exact-length repr(C) leading-field buffers with arbitrary contents and replacement values; they do not establish arbitrary-T, arbitrary allocation-context, invalid/short/misaligned-buffer, or Rust aliasing guarantees. These supplemental Kani checks are not among the 66 Aeneas machine claims.
current_report_fields.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, Charon/Aeneas, official scalar/byte primitives, Lean kernel, Kani and CBMC are trusted. Fifty native-endian std-operation models are explicitly supplied. Their Rust byte formulas and official Lean byte primitives are connected by review, not a mechanically checked cross-language theorem; std operator bodies are not independently proved in Lean. Kani and extraction use different Rust nightlies. The six bitwise results quantify arbitrary underlying operator dictionaries without proving user callback bodies. All 66 API contracts and 50 model specifications use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound as transitive axioms.
current_report_fields.limitations: Coverage is limited to six bitwise methods and sixty concrete integer From implementations on the stated target/model domain. The forty-six byte/slice APIs and their unsafe layout/validity/aliasing obligations are not covered by these Aeneas claims. No generic arbitrary-T memory-safety, other target, endian, or pointer-width claim is established. Derived standard-trait methods are excluded. Remaining trait/default/blanket behavior is not verified. Type-specialized Rust identities and any erased server catalogue keys must be distinguished.

report.title: Integer single-bit operations and generic slice routing, with exact failure cases
report.explanation: The unchanged bit_field 0.10.3 single-bit methods are verified for all twelve integer types: in-range indices read or update exactly that bit, returned mutable-reference writes propagate to the original value, and invalid indices fail at the assertion. All twelve primitive BIT_LENGTH values equal their widths. The original generic slice bit_length/get_bit/set_bit bodies are also composition-proved: assuming their declared BitField constant and per-element normal-return contracts, they use element index bit/width and local index bit%width, preserve other slice entries on update, and report zero-width/out-of-bounds errors. bit_length returns length times width or integerOverflow. Rust source and Cargo.toml are archive-identical.
report.trusted_assumptions: The official Rust/Charon/Aeneas translation and integer/slice models, Lean, and Kani/CBMC are trusted. The size_of model uses Lean-only PrimitiveRustLayout evidence with twelve supplied primitive instances, including pointer size8 on x86_64. The original generated Funs is unchanged: each of its twelve ground calls statically elaborates to the expected instance dictionary, checked explicitly. This added implicit evidence is not a Rust trait or an in-Lean proof of std layout. The Lean class remains extensible; coverage is the frozen twelve-call closure, not class sealing. Bool lacks an instance in the audited environment, and there is no supplied fallback for arbitrary types. Kani checks the same twelve actual layouts and all primitive single-bit/returned-reference behavior for arbitrary valid values. Connecting Kani Rust and Lean representations is a reviewed bridge, not an in-Lean std layout proof; Rust nightlies differ. Generic slice theorems assume the complete stated observation/update callback contracts, including the final state after returned-reference writeback. They do not prove arbitrary callback implementations. Mapped audits allow only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
report.limitations: Only twenty-four primitive single-bit methods, twelve width constants and three callback-conditional slice bodies are established. Primitive and slice get_bits/set_bits range methods remain unproved. A separately Kani-checked example shows signed range behavior differs from ordinary masked updates: 112_i8.set_bits(0..4,1) yields 1, changing high bits outside the range; the unsigned example yields 113. The verified single-bit methods are unaffected. Generic callback side effects, failure/divergence outside the stated contracts, other targets and release extraction are not established. No generic Rust size_of property, panic text or unwinding-state guarantee is claimed.

report.explanation: For rand_xoshiro 0.8.1, the unchanged native word-generating method of each of its fifteen generators returns Ok of the specified output scrambler and performs the exact documented word-state transition. Coverage includes SplitMix64, both xoroshiro64 variants, all three xoroshiro128 variants, and all three variants of each xoshiro128, xoshiro256 and xoshiro512 family. For 32-bit-word engines the native method is try_next_u32; for 64-bit-word engines it is try_next_u64. SplitMix64::try_next_u32 is also proved independently, including its distinct Mix4 output formula, among the direct body proofs. Each theorem covers arbitrary internal words, including all-zero states, and establishes normal termination in the Aeneas model. Array-state representation theorems establish that the four-word and eight-word inputs cover every valid fixed-length engine state. Exact output formulas and resulting fields are defined independently of the generated Rust body in the output*/next* specifications. The selected original bodies have byte-identical official Aeneas translations under the default and serde feature configurations, so these body guarantees apply to both configurations; this does not verify the serde trait implementations. Nine further 32-bit APIs are verified through exact forwarding selectors whose calls to the unchanged original API are inlined by the Rust compiler: all three xoroshiro128, all three xoshiro256 and all three xoshiro512 variants. These establish the same state transition as their 64-bit method, with low 32 output bits for xoroshiro128++ and xoroshiro128**, and high 32 bits for the other seven variants. The selector source, typed receiver/return correspondence, target, original method inline scopes and absence of unknown externals are guarded. Default and serde selected programs are byte-identical. Four additional direct body proofs cover Seed512: Default initializes all 64 bytes to zero; AsRef exposes exactly the stored bytes; AsMut exposes those bytes and writes back every legal 64-byte replacement unchanged; iter initializes the standard slice-iterator model over those same bytes at position zero. SplitMix64::state is additionally proved to return exactly the eight little-endian bytes of its complete internal u64 state, for every state including zero. All fifteen generators’ state methods are now covered: each returns the complete fixed-length little-endian bytes of every stored unsigned word in field order, for arbitrary internal word patterns including all-zero. Fourteen additional serializers bring the registered total to forty-four: thirty-five direct original bodies and nine compiler-inlined calls. The eight-word serializers also have a decreasing-measure proof that the original enumerate loop terminates after visiting each word. These are serialization results, not serde trait implementation proofs. Independent original-source Kani evidence additionally checks all fifteen from_seed APIs over their full fixed-size byte-seed domains, including the all-zero fallback, and all fifteen state serializers over every valid internal word pattern, including states that seeds may not reach. Default and serde configurations each pass fifteen seed harnesses/6014 checks and fifteen state harnesses/8024 checks. Five separate composition harnesses per configuration (892 checks) cover the remaining 32-bit-engine try_next_u64 operations against independent two-step little-endian output/poststate formulas. These ordinary Kani harnesses are separate tool guarantees, not extra Aeneas machine claims or a mechanized cross-tool equivalence; overlapping serializers are not counted twice. Read-only observers occur only as exact suffixes in generated measurement copies, with original production bytes preserved.

report.title: Exact integer writes and misuse checks in NoHashHasher
report.explanation: For nohash-hasher 0.2.0 on x86_64 with std enabled or disabled, Default initializes the stored value to zero, Clone preserves state, and finish returns the stored integer. Each of the ten integer write methods stores the Rust conversion of its input to u64: unsigned values are widened and signed values are converted modulo 2^64. With debug assertions enabled, the first integer write succeeds and a later write fails its assertion. With debug assertions disabled, each integer write replaces the stored value. The generic byte-slice write always panics in both configurations. These are exact per-method state and result contracts over all inputs, proved from unchanged published Rust bodies. Separate original-body Kani evidence checks handwritten Debug::fmt for NoHashHasher<u8> after Default or one arbitrary write_u8, using default {:?} formatting into a fixed 64-byte writer. Successful output has exact tuple delimiters, canonical decimal state and, in debug mode, the correct written flag. A writer that errors on its first call propagates Err and leaves its buffer unchanged. All std/no_std dependency and debug/release combinations pass separately: 2175 debug and 2143 release checks in each feature configuration; the verification harness itself uses std. This is a bounded formatter/input-domain supplement, not another Aeneas API claim or a proof for arbitrary stored u64 values, writers, formatting options or partial-write failures. A separate Kani supplement executes the actual standard Clone::clone_from default body and original manual Clone for NoHashHasher<u64>, in all four configurations. Source and destination independently begin at Default or one arbitrary write_u64. current_report_fields.explanation:
For oorandom 11.1.5, twelve original integer/state APIs have exact value/state proofs for every scalar input, including zero states and even restored increments. For both Rand32 and Rand64, new_inc sets increment to ((input_increment << 1) OR 1), advances from zero, adds the seed with wrapping arithmetic, then advances again; new uses DEFAULT_INC. state and from_state preserve the complete state/increment pair, with save/restore identity. Unsigned generation returns the specified PCG-XSH-RR permutation of the old state and advances to multiplier*state+increment modulo the state width. Signed generation returns the same output bits interpreted as i32/i64 and preserves that updated state. These calls terminate normally in the extracted model.

Separate Kani results cover both original rand_float methods for every complete state/increment pair. They return exactly n/2^24 or n/2^53, where n is the top24 or53 bits of the corresponding unsigned word, with the exact independent IEEE encoding and a value in [0,1). Their complete poststate equals an actual unsigned-word call. This follows from successful original-float/helper and all-word/helper specifications on the identical Rust helper; a direct Rand32 check independently confirms the same contract. State equality alone is not a call-count proof; original source/LLBC observations separately identify the sole word call.

Both original rand_range methods now have exact trace contracts in the extracted debug model. For valid width=end-start, each candidate consumes the next actual PCG word and advances the actual generator. If candidate n is accepted and every earlier candidate rejects against the proved canonical threshold, sampling returns exactly floor(product_n/2^b)+start and the candidate state after n+1 words, where b is32 or64. If every candidate rejects, it diverges. The classical first-accepted-or-all-rejected case split is exhaustive, not an executable termination decision. The specification’s auxiliary typed width must equal end.val-start.val. Invalid start>=end ranges produce assertion failure. Prior no-failure/normal-return bounds/increment preservation and the publicly restored(0,0) range0..3 divergence result remain included; constructor reachability of that pair is not claimed.

Additional Kani checks establish From<Self>, Borrow<Self> and BorrowMut<Self> identity and mutable replacement propagation for every public state/inc pair; Any matches its own TypeId and distinguishes Rand32 from Rand64 without changing state. CloneToUninit preserves the source and copies its complete state into a distinct valid aligned MaybeUninit stack slot.

Six generic conversion families have conditional original-body Lean contracts: Into delegates to From; TryInto forwards the complete TryFrom result; blanket TryFrom delegates to Into and wraps a normal result in Ok. report.title: CR/LF/CRLF normalization for finite character lists (adapted source)
report.explanation: For every finite character list, the Aeneas translation of normalize-line-endings 0.3.0's adapted normalized constructor and Iterator::next returns exactly the list obtained by replacing each CRLF pair and each remaining CR with LF, while preserving other characters. The proof uses a total, fused list iterator and an observation budget greater than the input length, with no fixed input bound. The output contains no CR, is no longer than the input, and is unchanged by another normalization pass. The constructor and next bodies are dependencies of the checked public theorem. Extraction required replacing three character patterns with equality guards. Kani additionally checks one-step equivalence of the actual original and adapted next bodies for both prior-state flags and all possible character replies in a non-panicking two-reply iterator trace model: returned value, adapter state, callback count, and remaining modeled iterator state agree. The Aeneas theorem applies to the adapted extraction. Separate original-source evidence now proves the unchanged normalized constructor directly with official Aeneas: for every translated iterator and Iterator dictionary it returns that iterator and initializes the previous-CR flag to false. This says nothing about later next calls. Independently, Kani checks original iterator outputs for lengths zero through four and every valid Unicode scalar value against an eager CR/LF/CRLF reference: exact output, no CR, nonincreasing length, idempotence, two exhausted None replies, and the initial inherited Iterator size_hint default. The Kani input iterator is total and finite; unwind bound eight retains unwinding assertions (437 successful checks). These original-source supplements are distinct from the one adapted-source machine claim.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, Charon/Aeneas translation, their standard-library models, and the Lean kernel are trusted; the supplementary equivalence result also trusts Kani/CBMC and its Rust compilation/modeling. The input iterator is modeled as consuming one character per successful call and returning None permanently after exhaustion. No additional local axioms are used; the public theorem depends only on Lean's propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
report.limitations: The original crates.io source is retained unchanged, but its character-pattern switches are unsupported by the pinned Aeneas translator. The three guard replacements have a Kani-checked one-step equivalence under the documented two-reply, non-panicking callback model. This is not a generic contextual-equivalence proof for every Rust Iterator implementation, nor a direct arbitrary-length Aeneas proof of the unmodified iterator next body. The original constructor alone is separately body-proved; bounded original iterator Kani behavior does not establish arbitrary-length or arbitrary-callback behavior. The end-to-end Aeneas guarantee remains scoped to the adapted extraction and total fused list iterator model. Arbitrary external iterators, their panics or divergence, and iterators that resume after None are outside the end-to-end theorem. No separate general memory-safety claim is made.

report.title: ASCII classification, string views and sequence updates
report.explanation: For ascii 1.1.0, as_byte returns the exact ASCII code for every valid AsciiChar. The eleven classification methods are correct for all 128 characters: digits are characters '0' through '9'; alphabetic is A-Z or a-z; alphanumeric additionally accepts digits; lowercase and uppercase accept a-z and A-Z respectively; hexdigit accepts 0-9, A-F or a-f. Graphic accepts byte codes 33-126 and printable accepts 32-126. Blank accepts space or tab; whitespace accepts space, tab, LF, CR and FF, rejecting vertical tab; control accepts codes 0-31 or 127. eq_ignore_ascii_case returns exactly whether the two codes are equal after mapping A-Z to a-z and leaving other codes unchanged; the independent mathematical equivalence is proved for all 128 squared valid pairs. For the AsciiChar implementation of ToAsciiChar, the checked method always returns Ok of the same value and the unchecked method returns that same value. is_ascii_punctuation accepts exactly ASCII intervals 33-47, 58-64, 91-96 and 123-126. The hand-written Default implementation returns the NUL enum value. AsAsciiStrError::valid_up_to returns its stored index; this does not establish that a separate validator found the first invalid byte. The public is_alphabetic, is_alphanumeric, is_lowercase and is_uppercase methods satisfy the same letter/digit predicates. is_whitespace accepts space, tab, LF, CR, VT and FF. For every u32 radix, is_digit returns normally at radix 0-36 and accepts exactly characters whose digit value (0-9 or case-independent A-Z values 10-35) is below the radix; other characters return false. Thus radix 0 always returns false and radix 1 accepts only character '0'. Every radix above 36 panics. The other twenty-three character/error bodies terminate normally in the model. AsciiStr::as_slice preserves the complete character sequence; as_mut_slice supplies that initial view and its generated backward function writes every valid same-length replacement back exactly. AsciiStr::len gives the exact sequence length and is_empty is equivalent to an empty sequence. For an already valid AsciiStr receiver, the AsAsciiStr checked conversion returns Ok with the unchanged view, its unchecked conversion is the same view, and the AsMutAsciiStr unchecked conversion preserves the initial view and exact same-length valid replacement writeback. These original implementations are identities, not raw byte casts or validation of other input types. AsciiString::new produces an empty sequence, len returns its exact length, and is_empty is equivalent to an empty sequence. push writes back the original sequence followed by the supplied character below the model length limit; at model length usizeMAX it fails with maximumSizeExceeded. Separately, Kani directly checked the original checked ToAsciiChar bodies for u8, i8, u16, u32 and char over their complete type domains: Ok exactly for ASCII-range inputs, preserving the codepoint, and Err otherwise. Those five body-check results are separate evidence and are not additional Lean API claims. Seven separate Kani checks also verify original case conversion and mutable writeback, as_char, case-insensitive equality and printable control pictures over all 128 valid characters (all pairs for equality). These establish A-Z/a-z mapping, exact receiver updates, ASCII code preservation and U+2400 control pictures with DEL at U+2421.
report.trusted_assumptions: Borrowed slice contracts use the generated value and backward-function semantics. They do not independently establish Rust pointer identity, lifetime or aliasing rules, and no resizing through a mutable slice is claimed. The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. Proofs split the complete finite AsciiChar type and use kernel-checked logical reduction and proved scalar arithmetic, without native-evaluation trust. The byte-code table contains each actual ASCII variant in code order. Transitive axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; no custom models or local axioms are introduced. Separate Kani body checks trust Kani/CBMC, their standard/intrinsic semantics and their pinned Rust compiler; no mechanized cross-tool equivalence is claimed.
report.limitations: Thirty-five API mappings are Lean-proved; the other explicitly described scalar/case results are separate Kani body checks. The identity proofs for unsafe methods apply only to their original AsciiChar and AsciiStr receiver implementations, which perform no raw cast. They establish nothing about unchecked conversions from integers, char, byte slices, str or other trait implementations. The Lean mathematical code-fold is not a proof of the separate case-conversion APIs; those original bodies instead have the separately recorded full-domain Kani checks. General input validation, the remaining AsciiStr/AsciiString APIs, allocation, serde and arbitrary unsafe conversions remain unproved. The official Vec model stores only element sequences and a length bound. It does not represent capacity, Rust isizeMAX allocation limits, allocator availability, OS failure or OOM. Thus the push result and failure partition are properties of that model; no exact physical allocation/panic behavior or capacity preservation is claimed. Case conversion and printable-picture behavior have separate Kani evidence, not Lean proofs. Invalid enum representations are outside the input domain. The original is_digit_strange_radixes test fails on the pinned modern Rust because char::is_digit panics at radix 0/1; the crate is_digit API is covered separately for all radix values; the failed test comparison invokes std char::is_digit at radix 0/1. Remaining original tests pass with only that test excluded. The five checked scalar conversion bodies and the stated case/character bodies have separate Kani evidence, rather than additional Lean claims. The original AsciiChar::new constructor is checked only on ASCII inputs by the generator; its non-ASCII panic domain remains unproved. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets were not proved.

current_report_fields.title: ASCII classification, string views and sequence updates
current_report_fields.explanation: For ascii 1.1.0, as_byte returns the exact ASCII code for every valid AsciiChar. The eleven classification methods are correct for all 128 characters: digits are characters '0' through '9'; alphabetic is A-Z or a-z; alphanumeric additionally accepts digits; lowercase and uppercase accept a-z and A-Z respectively; hexdigit accepts 0-9, A-F or a-f. Graphic accepts byte codes 33-126 and printable accepts 32-126. Blank accepts space or tab; whitespace accepts space, tab, LF, CR and FF, rejecting vertical tab; control accepts codes 0-31 or 127. eq_ignore_ascii_case returns exactly whether the two codes are equal after mapping A-Z to a-z and leaving other codes unchanged; the independent mathematical equivalence is proved for all 128 squared valid pairs. For the AsciiChar implementation of ToAsciiChar, the checked method always returns Ok of the same value and the unchecked method returns that same value. is_ascii_punctuation accepts exactly ASCII intervals 33-47, 58-64, 91-96 and 123-126. The hand-written Default implementation returns the NUL enum value. AsAsciiStrError::valid_up_to returns its stored index; this does not establish that a separate validator found the first invalid byte. The public is_alphabetic, is_alphanumeric, is_lowercase and is_uppercase methods satisfy the same letter/digit predicates. is_whitespace accepts space, tab, LF, CR, VT and FF. For every u32 radix, is_digit returns normally at radix 0-36 and accepts exactly characters whose digit value (0-9 or case-independent A-Z values 10-35) is below the radix; other characters return false. Thus radix 0 always returns false and radix 1 accepts only character '0'. Every radix above 36 panics. The other twenty-three character/error bodies terminate normally in the model. AsciiStr::as_slice preserves the complete character sequence; as_mut_slice supplies that initial view and its generated backward function writes every valid same-length replacement back exactly. AsciiStr::len gives the exact sequence length and is_empty is equivalent to an empty sequence. For an already valid AsciiStr receiver, the AsAsciiStr checked conversion returns Ok with the unchanged view, its unchecked conversion is the same view, and the AsMutAsciiStr unchecked conversion preserves the initial view and exact same-length valid replacement writeback. These original implementations are identities, not raw byte casts or validation of other input types. AsciiString::new produces an empty sequence, len returns its exact length, and is_empty is equivalent to an empty sequence. push writes back the original sequence followed by the supplied character below the model length limit; at model length usizeMAX it fails with maximumSizeExceeded. Separately, Kani directly checked the original checked ToAsciiChar bodies for u8, i8, u16, u32 and char over their complete type domains: Ok exactly for ASCII-range inputs, preserving the codepoint, and Err otherwise. Those five body-check results are separate evidence and are not additional Lean API claims. Seven separate Kani checks also verify original case conversion and mutable writeback, as_char, case-insensitive equality and printable control pictures over all 128 valid characters (all pairs for equality). These establish A-Z/a-z mapping, exact receiver updates, ASCII code preservation and U+2400 control pictures with DEL at U+2421. For every FromAsciiError<O> with arbitrary owner type O, ascii_error returns exactly its stored AsAsciiStrError and into_source consumes the wrapper and returns exactly its stored original owner. Both terminate normally with no Clone/Copy requirement on O and no validation or conversion. The stored error index is merely projected; these methods do not establish that a separate validator found an invalid byte. For the original default-allocator Vec<AsciiChar> implementations, From<Vec<AsciiChar>> for AsciiString, From<AsciiString> for Vec<AsciiChar>, and both IntoAsciiString methods preserve every character, its order and the sequence length in the official Vec model. The checked method returns Ok for every valid typed ASCII vector. The unchecked method returns the same wrapped vector for this exact implementation; its elements must already be valid AsciiChar values and it performs no raw-byte reinterpretation. These results do not validate Vec<u8> or describe physical allocation addresses, capacity or allocator failure behavior. Five further exact borrowing implementations are covered: AsRef<[AsciiChar]> and AsMut<[AsciiChar]> for AsciiStr and AsciiString preserve the complete initial character sequence and length; each mutable backward function writes every valid same-length replacement back exactly. AsRef<AsciiStr> for AsciiStr returns the unchanged typed view. These claims concern valid typed receivers and the modeled sequence, not physical buffer identity. Three further exact original methods are covered: AsMut<AsciiStr> for AsciiStr returns its unchanged typed view and identity backward function, so valid same-length replacements are written back exactly. ToAsciiCharError Error::description returns exactly "not an ASCII character" and AsAsciiStrError Error::description returns exactly "one or more bytes are not ASCII", for every error value. These descriptions do not validate the stored error or describe formatting behavior. The generic AsciiChar::from_ascii<C:ToAsciiChar> method exactly forwards the supplied checked callback result, preserving normal Ok/Err and modeled failure or divergence. It does not independently establish validation or termination of arbitrary callback implementations. For original FromAsciiError<O> Error::description (Rust O:Any), every owner and stored error index returns normally with the same exact constant one or more bytes are not ASCII, without inspecting or converting the owner. Separately, original-Rust Kani checks establish thirty additional scalar contracts: conversion of every valid AsciiChar to u8 or char preserves its code; equality and partial ordering against every u8 and every valid Unicode char agree with numeric code comparison in both directions, including inherited ne/lt/le/gt/ge on those manual implementations. Five further unsafe ToAsciiChar conversions for u8, i8, u16, u32 and char return the exact valid character for every documented safe input code 0..127. These thirty-five contracts are supplemental Kani evidence, not additional Lean API mappings.
current_report_fields.trusted_assumptions: Borrowed slice contracts use the generated value and backward-function semantics. They do not independently establish Rust pointer identity, lifetime or aliasing rules, and no resizing through a mutable slice is claimed. The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. Proofs split the complete finite AsciiChar type and use kernel-checked logical reduction and proved scalar arithmetic, without native-evaluation trust. The byte-code table contains each actual ASCII variant in code order. Transitive axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; no custom models or local axioms are introduced. current_report_fields.limitations: Fifty-one API mappings are Lean-proved; the other explicitly described scalar/case results are separate Kani body checks. The unsafe identity results cover only ToAsciiChar for AsciiChar, AsAsciiStr/AsMutAsciiStr for an existing AsciiStr, and IntoAsciiString for the original default-allocator Vec<AsciiChar>. report.title: Either branch operations and conditional callback composition
report.explanation: In the value model, left_or_default/right_or_default return the matching payload independently of the Default computation. On the opposite variant they delegate its exact modeled outcome. Separate theorems describe its returned value only under a normal-result premise and propagate modeled failure/divergence only under the corresponding premise. No particular Default value, failure freedom or termination is certified. The handwritten conversions between Result<R,L> and Either<L,R> preserve each payload: Result Ok becomes Either Right and Result Err becomes Either Left; the reverse maps Right to Ok and Left to Err. Every variant returns normally in the model, and both composition orders reconstruct the original value. The foreign self of the reverse implementation is core::result::Result<R,L>, not Either. Twelve callback APIs compose a supplied mathematical callback contract with variant selection. is_left_and/right_and apply the callback only to the indicated variant and otherwise return false; is_left_or/right_or return true on the indicated variant and apply the callback to the other. map_left/right map only the named payload and preserve the other variant and payload. map_left_or/right_or return the mapped named payload or the supplied default. left_or_else/right_or_else preserve the named payload or compute it from the opposite payload. left_and_then/right_and_then return the selected callback-produced Either unchanged, or preserve the opposite variant and payload. IntoEither::into_either chooses Left on true and Right on false, preserving the payload. IntoEither::into_either_with applies the predicate to the modeled borrowed payload and selects that branch from its mathematical result. The original impl<T> IntoEither for T has no overrides: its compiler-extracted dictionary is linked directly to the verified default, removing an extra dispatch assumption. Selected predicate failure propagates unchanged. The twelve inherent callback APIs use a normal-result premise for every callback argument; the IntoEither predicate theorem needs it only at the actual input. Separate companion theorems show selected callback failure is propagated unchanged and non-selected branches preserve their result without any callback success premise. For either 1.19.0 with default features on x86_64, the following value-semantic guarantees exclude payload destructor effects; they do not establish Rust panic freedom for arbitrary Drop implementations. In that model, is_left/is_right identify the actual branch; left/right return the corresponding optional payload; left_or/right_or select that payload or the given default; flip swaps the branch and a separate composition theorem proves flipping twice returns the original value. left_and/right_and select the supplied value or preserve the opposite payload. factor_none moves the optional payload outside Either while retaining its tag. factor_first/factor_second move the common tuple component outside Either. as_ref preserves the variant and referenced value; as_mut preserves the initial view and its generated backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back to the original variant. The earlier thirty named bodies return normally in the value model under their stated conditions. The two default-fallback methods instead retain the entire abstract Default outcome on the fallback branch; they can model-fail or model-diverge when that supplied computation does. Their matching-payload branch returns the payload without any Default success premise.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No additional axioms or custom models are assumed; callback behavior is an explicit premise of the conditional composition theorems. Reference contracts use Aeneas's value and backward-function semantics; they do not independently verify the compiler borrow checker or Rust aliasing model.
report.limitations: Default delegation is a value-model contract, not verification of the actual supplied Default implementation or of its value/termination/effects. Discarded Rust payload destructors can panic, fail to terminate or affect external state; their execution and unwind/return ordering are not modeled. The Default success/failure/divergence statements must not be read as a claim covering all such Rust Drop behavior. For IntoEither::into_either_with the remaining premise is normal modeled predicate behavior on the actual argument; its original conversion dispatch has been proved from the real blanket instance. This does not establish interior-mutability or external captured-state effects beyond the value/reference model. Callback termination, panic freedom, captured-state effects and concrete closure correctness are not established by these conditional composition proofs. The theorem hypotheses describe modeled FnOnce results; unchanged modeled failure propagation does not specify Rust panic payloads, unwinding or external effects. Only the thirty-two named methods and the two-flip composition are proved. Other inherent and callback-taking APIs, iterators, pinning, standard trait implementations and serde remain unproved. Rust destructor behavior and resource consumption are outside the pure value model. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets were not proved.

report.explanation: byteorder-lite 0.1.0: fixed-width unsigned and signed integer writes, plus BE/LE write_f32/write_f64, write their exact bit representations in the selected endian order and preserve trailing bytes when the output is long enough; shorter buffers panic before writing. Float proofs quantify over every 32/64-bit representation, including NaN payloads and signed zeros, under explicit bit-pattern and std to_bits models. No floating arithmetic is modeled. Signed write_i24 and write_int additionally serialize the low 24 or 8*nbytes bits for every signed input value, preserving suffix bytes; no signed representability condition is required. Invalid byte counts or short buffers panic as specified. Signed read_int/read_i24 additionally return the exact two-complement prefix decode at the selected width; all invalid counts and short inputs assert before sign extension. LittleEndian from_slice_u16/u32/u64/u128 and from_slice_i16/i32/i64/i128 additionally leave every slice unchanged on the verified little-endian target, including empty slices and all element values. Native LittleEndian from_slice_f32/f64 also preserve every memory bit under the existing representations, including NaN payloads and signed zeros; this is not a Rust floating PartialEq claim. The two handwritten Default methods always panic. The four variable-width unsigned writers additionally have exact byte-count/space guards, selected-byte output on success and assertion failure otherwise. Unsigned 24-bit readers/writers additionally have exact 3-byte decoding/serialization, a 24-bit value domain and complete short-buffer/value-overflow failures. Four unsigned variable-width readers decode the exact selected prefix under their complete byte-count/input-length guard, and assert otherwise. Eight concrete original 48-bit default methods are also verified: unsigned reads decode six bytes below 2^48; unsigned writes require a value below 2^48; signed reads decode six-byte two-complement values; signed writes truncate every i64 input to its low 48 bits. Enough buffer space preserves the suffix; short buffers fail assertion. Each original default body is connected by definitional equality to its original concrete general-width callee with count six.
report.limitations: This covers 34 selected writer methods, fourteen scoped integer readers, ten native-target identity conversions, and two handwritten Default methods, not all public APIs. Fixed-width 16/32/64/128-bit reads, remaining signed 128-bit variable-width wrappers, other bulk and in-place conversions, I/O extensions, other targets and release extraction remain unproved. The float result establishes bit serialization only: floating arithmetic, comparisons, rounding, numeric accuracy, NaN arithmetic and signaling behavior are not modeled. Kani public-writer buffer lengths are fixed at 6 and 10; arbitrary valid slice lengths are quantified separately by the Lean theorems. The write_int documentation says nonrepresentable values panic, while original-body theorems establish truncation for all i64 inputs when count/space guards hold; 176 finite native observations corroborate selected boundaries. This is a documentation/behavior mismatch, not a memory-safety finding. write_i24 documents only short-buffer panic and is not classified as a documentation problem. Other signed reads remain unproved. Opposite-endian conversion methods and other target configurations are not covered by the identity results. Panic messages and unwinding side effects are not specified.

Signed read_int/read_i24 additionally return the exact two-complement prefix decode at the selected width; all invalid counts and short inputs assert before sign extension. LittleEndian from_slice_u16/u32/u64/u128 and from_slice_i16/i32/i64/i128 additionally leave every slice unchanged on the verified little-endian target, including empty slices and all element values. The two handwritten Default methods always panic. The four variable-width unsigned writers additionally have exact byte-count/space guards, selected-byte output on success and assertion failure otherwise. Unsigned 24-bit readers/writers additionally have exact 3-byte decoding/serialization, a 24-bit value domain and complete short-buffer/value-overflow failures. Four unsigned variable-width readers decode the exact selected prefix under their complete byte-count/input-length guard, and assert otherwise. Eight concrete original 48-bit default methods are also verified: unsigned reads decode six bytes below 2^48; unsigned writes require a value below 2^48; signed reads decode six-byte two-complement values; signed writes truncate every i64 input to its low 48 bits. Enough buffer space preserves the suffix; short buffers fail assertion. Each original default body is connected by definitional equality to its original concrete general-width callee with count six. BE/LE read_int128 and write_int128 also cover all values and counts: signed reads decode the selected prefix for counts1..16 with enough input and assert otherwise; signed writes serialize the low8*count bits of every i128, preserving suffix bytes. Invalid write counts0 or above16 fail integerOverflow in unextend_sign128 before the writer; valid counts with insufficient output assert.
